input.question: Was Pangaea an accident or necessary?
input.ground_truth: Sure it would be possible for there to be multiple continents without having a Pangea first. It is possible to have a world with absolutely no active tectonics. In fact Earth may be very unusual in this respect, we don't know yet. A super continent is in no way a prerequisite for separate continents to eventually exist, it is just the way it happened on our planet to the best of our knowledge. Also our separate continents may eventually combine again to become a second Pangea.

Okay! Imagine the Earth is like a big, stretchy playdough ball.

Long, long ago—like, a *super* long time ago—pieces of the Earth were all stuck together to make one big land called Pangaea. It wasn’t because someone dropped it or made a mistake (so it wasn’t an accident), and it wasn’t just a lucky thing that happened by chance either.

It happened because the Earth’s crust (that’s the outside layer of the Earth, like the skin on an apple) moves around slowly. This moving is called “plate tectonics.” The pieces, called plates, bump into each other, pull apart, and stick together over millions and millions of years.

So Pangaea happened because of how the Earth works—it was kind of necessary, like how snow melts when it gets warm. It’s just what happens when the Earth’s crust moves and changes over a really, really long time!
